scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original independent letter comprehension B2 draft, not approved.

tabs.title: Appearance and Reality
tabs.description: Interpret Lena's experience of life abroad.

tabs.title: Building Connections
tabs.description: Analyse why encounters change her understanding.

tabs.title: Rebuilding Friendship
tabs.description: Evaluate the message's purpose and alternatives.

questions.q: Why does Lena describe her social-media updates as an incomplete picture?
choices: They contained inaccurate information about the city.
They showed attractive moments while concealing her loneliness.
She had posted photographs of places she never visited.
Her friends had misunderstood the local language.
questions.explanation: Lena contrasts cheerful captions with her difficulties settling in.

questions.q: What was missing from Lena's early experience despite her knowledge of Rotterdam?
choices: Directions to important city museums.
A friendly place to buy food in the morning.
A family willing to let her stay.
Someone she could contact when she needed emotional support.
questions.explanation: She could navigate the city but did not know whom to call after a bad day.

questions.q: Why does the old school photograph prompt Lena to rethink her messages?
choices: It reminds her of a friendship based on sharing difficulties, not just achievements.
It reveals that Alex has moved back to their old school.
It shows that she forgot the date of their final exam.
It convinces her that social media is never useful.
questions.explanation: Lena recalls that they used to share difficult experiences and realises she knows little about Alex's year.

questions.q: What is the significance of the woman describing bus routes as a secret language?
choices: The woman knows an invented language that Lena wants to study.
The local buses use a code that only residents can read.
Her practical confusion helps Lena recognise a shared feeling of being new.
The interview reveals that the bus system does not operate.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the interviewee's experience with her own embarrassment and uncertainty.

questions.q: What do the three listeners' reactions to the bakery interview suggest?
choices: The programme has become the most popular radio show in the city.
Experiences of not belonging are more common than they first appear.
The bakery owner has decided to stop teaching newcomers.
People generally dislike hearing about migration.
questions.explanation: Other listeners recognise their own stories in the interview.

questions.q: Why does Lena value the unpaid radio work more than the certificate?
choices: It allows her to avoid all academic work.
She believes all certificates are misleading.
She plans to become a professional bus driver.
The meaningful conversations help her feel part of a community.
questions.explanation: Lena explicitly values the relationships and stories over formal recognition.

questions.q: Why does Lena apologise for how her messages may have affected Alex?
choices: Her carefully chosen updates could have made their friendship feel one-sided.
She sent Alex too many long personal letters.
She asked Alex to work at the radio station without pay.
She forgot to book a train ticket for Alex.
questions.explanation: Lena acknowledges presenting a simplified version of her life and not asking about Alex.

questions.q: Why does Lena offer a regular call if Alex cannot travel?
choices: She wants Alex to edit her radio programme remotely.
She believes travelling by train is always unsafe.
Maintaining an honest conversation matters more than attending the event.
She has decided to cancel the storytelling evening.
questions.explanation: The alternative keeps the main goal of reconnecting achievable.

questions.q: What does Lena mean by not wanting another photograph of them looking happy?
choices: She no longer wants anyone to take photographs in Rotterdam.
She thinks Alex has become a bad photographer.
She wants to delete every picture from school.
She prefers genuine contact over an image that merely suggests closeness.
questions.explanation: The closing paragraph contrasts real conversation with a staged happy image.

questions.q: Which reply from Alex would best address Lena's underlying invitation?
choices: A collection of recent selfies without any written message.
An honest account of how Alex is doing and whether a visit or call is possible.
A request to forward the radio station's certificate.
A promise to visit without checking availability.
questions.explanation: Lena asks for Alex's real news and a practical way to connect.
